\title{A Nonasymptotic Good-Collar Bound on $\SU$\\
\large Finite-time prefactors and the one-link ultraviolet threshold}
\author{}
\date{20 July 2026}
\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
For the one-link heat-kernel conditional law with $m$ coherent staples, we
derive an explicit finite-time bad-curvature bound.  The estimate combines
radial monotonicity of the central $\SU$ heat kernel, exact Haar ball volume,
and a controlled Poisson-image ratio.  It upgrades a small-time rate theorem
by retaining every prefactor.  At $\rho=0.0082$, $\eta=0.001$, and $m=6$, the
bound crosses the degree-$18$ connected-set weight at
$t\simeq8.9942\times10^{-7}$; at $t=3\times10^{-6}$ its prefactor makes it
trivial.  The result assumes a coherent staple collar and does not estimate
the probability of collar failure.
\end{abstract}

\section{Heat-kernel input}

Identify $\SU$ with the unit three-sphere and write $\theta=d(I,g)\in[0,\pi]$.
The heat kernel for generator $\tfrac12\Delta$ is central, so it is denoted
$p_t(\theta)$.

\begin{lemma}[Radial monotonicity]
For every $t>0$, $p_t(\theta)$ is nonincreasing on $[0,\pi]$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For smooth radially decreasing approximations to the point mass, the radial
heat equation on $S^3$ is
\[
 \partial_t u=\tfrac12(u_{\theta\theta}+2\cot\theta\,u_\theta).
\]
Differentiate on compact subintervals of $(0,\pi)$ and apply the parabolic
maximum principle to the positive part of $u_\theta$, using the symmetry
boundary values at $0$ and $\pi$.  Radial decrease is preserved.  Passing to
the heat-kernel limit gives the assertion.
\end{proof}

For $0\leq\theta\leq R<\pi/2$, the paired Poisson-image representation gives
\begin{equation}
 p_t(\theta)=C_t\,\frac{\theta}{\sin\theta}
 e^{-\theta^2/(2t)}(1+r_t(\theta)),\qquad |r_t(\theta)|\leq q_t(R)<1.
 \label{eq:image}
\end{equation}
The executable certificate bounds $q_t(R)$ by a convergent image tail.  Put
\[
 c_t(R)=\frac{1+q_t(R)}{1-q_t(R)}.
\]
Equation \eqref{eq:image} implies
\begin{align}
 \frac{p_t(\rho)}{p_t(0)}
 &\leq \frac{\rho}{\sin\rho}c_t(R)e^{-\rho^2/(2t)},\label{eq:r1}\\
 \frac{p_t(0)}{p_t(r_0)}
 &\leq c_t(R)e^{r_0^2/(2t)}.\label{eq:r2}
\end{align}

\section{Finite-time theorem}

Let staples $S_i$ lie in a common $\eta$-ball centered at $C$.  After setting
$V=UC$ and $Q_i=C^{-1}S_i$, the conditional law is proportional to
$\prod_{i=1}^m p_t(VQ_i)\dd V$, with $d(I,Q_i)\leq\eta$.  For target $j$ let
$B_j(\rho)=\{V:d(I,VQ_j)\geq\rho\}$.

The normalized Haar volume of the ball $d(I,V)\leq\delta$ is
\begin{equation}
 v(\delta)=\frac{\delta-\tfrac12\sin(2\delta)}{\pi}.
 \label{eq:volume}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Nonasymptotic coherent-collar bound]
Assume
\[
 R=\max\{\rho,\eta+\delta\}<\pi/2,
 \qquad \rho^2>m(\eta+\delta)^2.
\]
Then, uniformly over all coherent staple families,
\begin{equation}
 \gamma_{t,S}(B_j(\rho))\leq
 \frac1{v(\delta)}\frac{\rho}{\sin\rho}c_t(R)^{m+1}
 \exp\!\left[-\frac{\rho^2-m(\eta+\delta)^2}{2t}\right].
 \label{eq:main}
\end{equation}
The right side may always be replaced by its minimum with one.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
On $B_j(\rho)$, radial monotonicity bounds the target factor by $p_t(\rho)$
and every other factor by $p_t(0)$.  Thus the numerator is at most
$p_t(\rho)p_t(0)^{m-1}$ because normalized Haar volume is one.  In the ball
$d(I,V)\leq\delta$, the triangle inequality gives
$d(I,VQ_i)\leq\eta+\delta$, so the normalization is at least
$v(\delta)p_t(\eta+\delta)^m$.  Divide, insert
\eqref{eq:r1}--\eqref{eq:r2}, and simplify.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
The auxiliary $\delta$ is a proof parameter.  The reported golden-section
search returns an admissible value and makes no theorem of global numerical
optimality.  Every returned probability remains rigorous for its selected
$\delta$.
\end{remark}

\section{Calibration and decision}

For $m=6$, $\rho=0.0082$, $\eta=0.001$, $\alpha=0.1$, and $\Delta=18$, the
critical connected-set weight is
\[
 q_{\rm crit}=e^{-\alpha}\Delta^{-2}=0.00279270808036.
\]
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}lr@{}}
\toprule
quantity & value\\
\midrule
frozen time & $3.0\times10^{-6}$\\
selected frozen $\delta$ & $8.22875586\times10^{-4}$\\
frozen raw log bound & $14.97453169$\\
finite-time probability upper bound & $1$\\
crossing time for $q_{\rm crit}$ & $8.99420304\times10^{-7}$\\
crossing $\delta$ & $3.36486781\times10^{-4}$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The favorable exponential rate at the frozen witness is insufficient after
the denominator-volume prefactor is restored.  The theorem nevertheless
gives a concrete smaller-time regime where the one-link conditional estimate
meets the desired counting weight.

\section{Frontier boundary}

The theorem is finite-volume, nonasymptotic, noncommutative, and gauge
covariant through the common-ball condition.  It does not show that coherent
collars occur under arbitrary adaptive histories.  It also does not control
multi-link integration, repeated RG, continuum limits, or a Hamiltonian gap.
The result is therefore a C2 restricted theorem.
